correctness.rationale: Verified n≥3, intrinsic 2n−2 dimensional Euclidean normalization and Exp(2) rate convention. The transportation/Hall constraints p_i+q_i≤1 are necessary for singleton rows and sufficient since any ≥2 rows reach every column. Uniform-simplex Beta(1,n−1) marginals give Pr(p_i+q_i>1)=1/binom(2n−2,n−1); two strict violations cannot coexist, proving exact volume ratio. For deleted (e_i,e_i), Cauchy–Schwarz yields min squared distance n/[2(n−1)] with an explicit equal-weight Q coupling; convexity of distance(Q,.) forces a P vertex to be farthest, proving Hausdorff. Centered independent Gaussians divided by R∼χ_{2n−2} give uniform intrinsic spherical direction. Direct support maxima over i≠j prove Δ=[1_{I+}min(top gaps)+1_{I−}min(bottom gaps)]/R. Independent uniform ranking permutations give Pr(I+)=Pr(I−)=1/n and Pr(I+∩I−)=1/[n(n−1)], independent of gaps and R; hence exact positive probability 2/n−1/[n(n−1)]. With b_n=Φ^{-1}(1−1/n)>0, the Gaussian tail ratio shows b_n times each top gap converges to Exp(1), and the minimum of two independent limits is Exp(2). The double-coincidence case has conditional probability 1/(2n−3)→0, while R/√(2n)→1. Gaussian increasing hazard and a superpolynomial small lower-second-maximum exceptional event supply uniform integrability of first two scaled-gap moments; inverse χ moments of R supply the normalizer control. The positive part contributes EΔ∼1/[n b_n√(2n)] and EΔ²∼1/[2 n² b_n²]; subtracting (EΔ)² preserves the variance equivalent. Independent implementation: n=3,4,5 intrinsic ConvexHull ratios 0.5,0.8,13/14 and squared distance n/[2(n−1)]; 3900 fresh support identities, exact-permutation rarity simulations n=8,20,50,100,200; one-event scaled-gap moments n=30,100,500 show slow convergence but expected trend. Computations are corroboration, not all-n proof.
residual_risks: Finite numerical Hull/SLSQP tests are floating point and check only n≤5; the universal theorem depends on the analytic Hall/convexity/spacing proofs.

For the moment asymptotics, the uniform-integrability tail estimate is sketched in source but reconstructible from normal increasing hazard and exponential lower-order-statistic exceptional event; not formally certified.
Affine transformations away from the stated intrinsic Euclidean embedding invalidate the metric constants.

originality.rationale: The natural sign-reversed bipartite root-polytope realization is indeed covered as an OBJECT by Almousa–Dochtermann–Smith, but their theorem family is tropical subdivisions, type ideals and toric edge-ring invariants (arXiv:2209.09851, §§1.1, 4.5, 5). The Ohsugi–Tsuchiya PQ adjacency polytope includes every diagonal vertex by definition (arXiv:2103.15045, p.1, §1), so its Ehrhart/normalized-volume formulas are for another hull and do not imply this diagonal-deleted random-width law. A published crown-graph symmetric-edge inball theorem uses the centrally symmetrized ± root hull, and proves radius/contact-facet phases rather than the one-sided P/Q directional width defect. Standard Gaussian extreme-order spacing is an acknowledged ingredient; the specific combination of exact volume, Hausdorff, Gaussian ranking event and conditional Exp(2) law has no dominating prior theorem in the inspected texts or Resultary results. This is best-of-knowledge and does not assert absolute novelty.
residual_risks: The volume and Hausdorff formulas may be independently known in older graph-root-polytope literature; these alone are not the claimed new angular law.
An unindexed probabilistic normal-cone or permutation-coupling treatment may state the same exact rarity and conditional gap theorem as a corollary; no complete worldwide priority guarantee.
Conclusions about prior PDF coverage are limited to the full text read and theorem sections actually inspected, not an assertion of absence in every historical source.

value.rationale: The crown root polytope Q_n is a canonical naturally defined deletion of a perfect matching of n vertices from the n²-vertex product Δ_{n−1}×Δ_{n−1}. Comparing three non-equivalent and motivated quantitative notions of geometric stability is useful: relative volume loss is exponentially small, Hausdorff gap tends to 1/√2, while random-direction width deficit appears with only Θ(1/n) probability and has a sharp conditional nondegenerate exponential scale. The exact objectwise formula and infinite-n limiting distribution form a self-contained structural separation, not a routine one-parameter renaming, arbitrary tiny table entry or unsupported numerical curiosity. Even if the elementary volume coefficient had been previously tabulated, the matching of exact rare-angle probability to extreme-order-statistic geometry is a motivated independent invariant with likely use in stability and random support-function comparisons.
residual_risks: The result is special to one canonical graph-deletion family and a fixed Euclidean metric; no broad stability theorem for arbitrary deletions is claimed.
Some ingredients are standard (Hall, Gaussian order spacings); value rests on the complete coupled three-metric result.

limitations: No formal machine-checked universal proof or external expert attestation claimed.
Novelty is best-of-knowledge after primary-text and Resultary comparisons; possible unindexed equivalence remains.
